newsitem.title: UK: Sterling reaches 1996 high against the mark.
newsitem.headline: Sterling reaches 1996 high against the mark.

text.p: The pound rose against the mark on Friday to hit its highest level this year, boosted by mark weakness and a buoyant gilt market, dealers said Friday.
It eclipsed the July peak of 2.3822 marks to trade at levels not seen since February 1995. It was at 2.3840 at 1453 GMT.
Broad-based mark weakness against most other European currencies and against the dollar helped buoy the pound, dealers and analysts said.
The German currency was hit by a wave of selling this week amid a fresh wave of optimism about a punctual start for European monetary union in 1999.
Sterling also traded at three-year highs against the yen above 173 yen, its highest level since April 1993.
UK government bond-related purchases by Japanese investors, attracted by the comparatively high yield of UK government bonds, also underpinned the pound against the yen, dealers said.

Sterling's outlook remains positive, analysts said. "I don't expect the pound to face much downward pressure at those levels given its positive fundamental and technical outlook," said James McKay, international economist at Paine Webber in London.
Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London, agreed: "We are bullish about the pound, given the improved UK current account and growth data and a positive technical outlook."
